new_spots.name: St Clair Beach
new_spots.bio: Dunedin's most popular beach, with an esplanade of cafes and bars, a heated salt-water pool on its western headland and a summer surf school.

new_spots.name: St Kilda Beach
new_spots.bio: The eastern stretch of Ocean Beach, a three-kilometre sweep of sand for swimming, surfing and walks that sea lions, seals and blue penguins regularly visit.

new_spots.name: Dunedin Botanic Garden
new_spots.bio: A 30-hectare garden at the north end of the city with an aviary, rhododendron, azalea and rose gardens and glasshouses, free to enter.

new_spots.name: Olveston
new_spots.bio: A Jacobean-style Edwardian mansion built for the Theomin family and furnished as it was in their day, entered on a one-hour guided tour.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: olveston.co.nz blocked scripts (403); left null. Price is Wikivoyage's adult guided-tour fee (Jan 2025), garden free

new_spots.name: Speight's Brewery
new_spots.bio: A Dunedin landmark since 1876, with guided brewery tours that finish with a 25-minute beer tasting.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: speights.co.nz loads but its title is only the beer brand ('Homepage - Speight's'), not the brewery tour; left null. Prices are Wikivoyage tour $45, tour with lunch $79

new_spots.name: Dunedin Chinese Garden
new_spots.bio: A late Ming to early Qing style scholar's garden built in Shanghai and reassembled in Dunedin, the only traditional Chinese garden in the Southern Hemisphere.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: dunedinchinesegarden.com blocked scripts (403); left null. Adult price from Wikivoyage

photo.file: Lan Yuan, Dunedin Chinese Garden - Dunedin, NZ - 24.jpg

new_spots.name: First Church
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia First Church of Otago infobox
new_spots.bio: An English-cathedral-style Presbyterian church of Oamaru stone built in 1868-73, with a 56 m spire.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: loaded; title 'First Church of Otago', H1 'Welcome to First Church of Otago'

new_spots.name: St Paul's Cathedral
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia St Paul's Cathedral, Dunedin infobox
new_spots.bio: An Oamaru-stone Anglican cathedral on the Octagon, begun in 1915 and consecrated in 1919, with a modernist chancel added in 1969-71.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: loaded; title 'St Paul's Cathedral, Dunedin', H1 welcomes to St Paul's Cathedral. Interior hours not confirmed after the 2020 roof fire, so hours are exterior only

photo.file: Wide shot of side of St Paul’s Cathedral, from the Octagon, Dunedin.jpg

new_spots.name: The Octagon
new_spots.bio: The eight-sided heart of the city, with a Robert Burns statue unveiled in 1887 and the Town Hall, Art Gallery and St Paul's Cathedral around it.

photo.file: The Octagon, Dunedin, Otago, South Island.jpg

new_spots.name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia Dunedin Public Art Gallery infobox
new_spots.bio: New Zealand's first art gallery, founded in 1884, with a rich historic collection that includes the only Monet in a New Zealand collection.

new_spots.name: Cargill's Castle
new_spots.bio: The ruins of an Italianate mansion completed in 1877 on a clifftop above St Clair, seen from outside as the site is not open to the public.

new_spots.name: Signal Hill
new_spots.bio: A 393 m hill north of the harbour head whose lookout gives views over the city, Otago Harbour and the peninsula.

new_spots.name: Mount Cargill
new_spots.bio: A volcanic peak dominating northern Dunedin, with panoramic views of the city, harbour and peninsula from its 676 m summit.

new_spots.name: Organ Pipes
new_spots.coordinates_source: Commons geotag of 'View across tops of Organ Pipes rock pillars.jpg' (taken at the formation)
new_spots.bio: Columnar basalt pillars set in a hillside, reached by a steep bush track from a car park on North Road, with views over the valley.

photo.file: View across tops of Organ Pipes rock pillars.jpg

new_spots.name: Orokonui Ecosanctuary
new_spots.coordinates_source: OSM Nominatim information/office 'Orokonui Ecosanctuary', 600 Blueskin Road
new_spots.bio: A 307-hectare pest-fenced sanctuary near Waitati where kaka, tui, bellbirds, tuatara and kiwi live in native bush.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: orokonui.org.nz blocked scripts (403/000); left null. Prices from Wikivoyage: self-guided $26, guided tour $65

new_spots.name: Port Chalmers
new_spots.bio: Dunedin's deep-water port town, 13 km along the harbour, with bluestone churches, a small maritime museum and lookouts over the water.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: portchalmers.com is a community site, not checked; left null

new_spots.name: Aramoana
new_spots.bio: A small seaside settlement at the mouth of Otago Harbour, with a quiet beach, a salt marsh and a mole running out along the harbour entrance.

photo.file: New Zealand Sea Lions at The Spit, Aramoana.jpg

new_spots.name: Glenfalloch Gardens
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia Glenfalloch Gardens infobox (rounded to arc-seconds)
new_spots.bio: A garden of national significance on Otago Peninsula, with woodland tracks through 30 acres, a 1000-year-old matai and a restaurant on site.
new_spots.ticketUrl_checked: loaded; title 'Glenfalloch Gardens | Wedding Venue Dunedin, Dining & Events', H1 'Discover Glenfalloch'. Wikivoyage gives $3 adult entry but dated Jan 2020, so cost omitted

new_spots.name: Allans Beach
new_spots.bio: A white-sand beach on the seaward side of the spit at the entrance to Hoopers Inlet, 25 km by road from the city centre.

photo.file: Mount Charles, Allans Beach, and Cape Saunders.jpg

new_spots.name: Victory Beach
new_spots.bio: The longest beach on Otago Peninsula, 3.2 km of sand named for the SS Victory, wrecked there in 1861.

new_spots.name: Warrington Beach
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia Warrington, New Zealand infobox (settlement beside the beach; beach point unverified)
new_spots.bio: A beach beside the small settlement of Warrington on Blueskin Bay, patrolled by lifeguards on summer weekends.

new_spots.name: Brighton Beach
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia Brighton, New Zealand infobox (town centre beside the beach)
new_spots.bio: A seaside town 20 km southwest of the city centre on the Southern Scenic Route, with a beach patrolled by lifeguards in summer.

new_spots.name: University of Otago
new_spots.bio: New Zealand's oldest university, whose Clocktower Building and other old campus buildings are worth a wander.

new_spots.name: Sandymount
new_spots.coordinates_source: Wikipedia Sandymount (New Zealand) infobox (hill; trailhead not source-verified)
new_spots.bio: A hill on Otago Peninsula whose eastern cliffs drop to chasms, among them Lover's Leap, 224 m high, and The Chasm.
